original_test_intent: Install the approved NIC driver on the authoritative target OS and verify correct device enumeration/binding/version with no platform-native device or event errors and restored network function.
original_method: Engineering selects Windows or Linux branch and supplies signed compatible package; agent records baseline, validates provenance/compatibility, runs vendor-supported tracked install and optional approved reboot, verifies device/driver/network/log state and leaves rollback to the recovery owner.
manual_activity: Engineer selects OS branch/package/reboot/rollback; operator maintains independent recovery; agent may stage and install only the approved signed package.
required_inputs: Authoritative Windows or Linux OS/build/kernel and target NIC/PCI/firmware matrix
Expected driver binding/version/device-manager or Linux module/network acceptance
Independent OOB/console, outage/reboot approval, backup/rollback, recovery and invalid-run policy
safety_requirements: Validate signature/checksum and exact OS/kernel/NIC compatibility before staging
Snapshot current driver/package/network state and prove independent recovery

Capture complete platform-native device/binding/version/network/event evidence and report reboot need
Do not choose OS/package, download arbitrary driver, continue after failure, recover automatically or issue verdict

Review final state and issue verdict

review_improvement: Prevents an invented Linux workflow from satisfying Windows-specific acceptance and makes the high-risk driver change auditable and recoverable.
independent_technical_reasoning: Driver installation semantics differ fundamentally by platform: Windows PnP/Device Manager state and signed INF packages are not equivalent to Linux modules, DKMS and kernel ABI compatibility. Because replacing a shared driver can remove the very interface used for remote control, package identity, affected devices and an independent recovery path must be fixed before any command is valid.
